S00_env_check.about: Check GPU, packages and internet, find the dataset, confirm val/ is empty, and confirm the Kaggle data and folds are identical to splits/folds_v1.csv.

S00_env_check_r2.about: Re-run of S00_env_check after pooling Kaggle's val/ folder (104 training femurs) back into train: confirms the Kaggle data and folds are now identical to splits/folds_v1.csv and that every file is found.

S01_yolov8s_seg_1024.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S01_yolov8s_seg_1024.about: Baseline 1: the base article's final model (YOLOv8-small-seg, 1024 px) retrained on our 5 folds with the paper's 100 epochs and Ultralytics defaults (batch 8 at 1024 px). Final weights, val=False during training, fracture threshold fitted on the out-of-fold predictions; every fold model also predicts the test set (fixed baseline = frozen configuration).

S02_yolov8s_seg_640.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S02_yolov8s_seg_640.about: Baseline 2: the paper's best-Dice setting (YOLOv8-small-seg, 640 px; test Dice .780 in its grid), same protocol as S01 with Ultralytics' default batch 16.

S03_yolo11s_seg_1024.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S03_yolo11s_seg_1024.about: Baseline 3: the newer YOLO11-small-seg at 1024 px with exactly S01's protocol (100 epochs, batch 8, Ultralytics defaults, final weights, OOF threshold), so it differs from S01 only in the architecture. Answers the reviewer question whether a newer YOLO closes the gap.

S00_net_check.gpu: T4 x2 (two networks at a time)
S00_net_check.about: Pre-flight of the 7 networks of S04-S10 on the real GPUs, before any of them is trained: downloads the ImageNet weights, finds the largest micro-batch that fits in a T4 (gradients are accumulated to the batch of 16), times a training step, and estimates the minutes per fold and per run. Also builds the resized image cache once and times it. Trains nothing.

S04_densenet121.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S04_densenet121.about: Baseline 4: DenseNet121 image classifier (6 classes), the article's best classifier (test AUC .993, 6-class accuracy 83.8%, Table 3), retrained on our 5 folds with the shared recipe (768 x 512 px, 60 epochs, AdamW, final weights, OOF threshold).
S04_densenet121.estimate_note: measured by S00_net_check (register line 5): micro-batch 16 x 1, 8.48 GB, 0.4813 s per micro-step, about 28.6 min per fold; 3 rounds of folds + about 5 min set-up

S05_efficientnet_b4.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S05_efficientnet_b4.about: Baseline 5: EfficientNet-B4 image classifier, an article baseline (test AUC .990, accuracy 79.0%, Table 3), same recipe as S04.
S05_efficientnet_b4.estimate_note: measured by S00_net_check (register line 5): micro-batch 8 x 2, 7.48 GB, 0.3387 s per micro-step, about 39.8 min per fold; 3 rounds of folds + about 5 min set-up (micro-batch 16 needed 14.58 GB, over 85% of the T4)

S06_convnext_tiny.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S06_convnext_tiny.about: Baseline 6 = A0 of Paper A: ConvNeXt-Tiny image classifier, the backbone of M0 and of both papers' models, same recipe as S04. Separates the effect of the new heads (Paper A) and of the reference image (Paper B) from the backbone.
S06_convnext_tiny.estimate_note: measured by S00_net_check (register line 5): micro-batch 16 x 1, 8.3 GB, 0.508 s per micro-step, about 30.1 min per fold; 3 rounds of folds + about 5 min set-up

S07_unet_r34.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S07_unet_r34.about: Baseline 7: U-Net with a ResNet34 encoder, semantic segmentation into the 6 classes (class of a femur = class of its predicted fracture region), same recipe. Standard segmentation baseline for the Dice comparison with YOLO (RQ1).
S07_unet_r34.estimate_note: measured by S00_net_check (register line 5): micro-batch 16 x 1, 8.38 GB, 0.5252 s per micro-step, about 31.5 min per fold; 3 rounds of folds + about 5 min set-up

S08_deeplabv3p_r34.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S08_deeplabv3p_r34.about: Baseline 8: DeepLabV3+ with a ResNet34 encoder, same task and recipe as S07.
S08_deeplabv3p_r34.estimate_note: measured by S00_net_check (register line 5): micro-batch 16 x 1, 6.25 GB, 0.447 s per micro-step, about 27.0 min per fold; 3 rounds of folds + about 5 min set-up

S09_segformer_b2.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S09_segformer_b2.about: Baseline 9: SegFormer (MiT-B2 transformer encoder), same task and recipe as S07.
S09_segformer_b2.estimate_note: measured by S00_net_check (register line 5): micro-batch 8 x 2, 10.58 GB, 0.5401 s per micro-step, about 63.3 min per fold; 3 rounds of folds + about 5 min set-up (micro-batch 16 ran out of memory)

S10_m0_convnext_unet.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
S10_m0_convnext_unet.about: Core model M0 (= A1 of Paper A = R0 of Paper B): U-Net with the ConvNeXt-Tiny encoder of S06, a binary fracture mask and the same 6-class head on the encoder's last features. Differs from S06 only by the decoder and its mask loss, so S06 vs S10 answers whether segmentation as an extra task helps.
S10_m0_convnext_unet.estimate_note: measured by S00_net_check (register line 5): micro-batch 16 x 1, 11.19 GB, 0.9139 s per micro-step, about 53.8 min per fold; 3 rounds of folds + about 5 min set-up

A6_dev_base.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
A6_dev_base.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); SLG-Net's heads add little; + pre-flight, image cache and the oracle predictions
A6_dev_base.about: Paper A fold-0 development (Analysis/06 §4). SLG-Net A6 with the base settings of Analysis/06 §2: teacher forcing over 30 epochs, region pooling at 1/16 and 1/32, the decision losses reach the mask. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the oracle test.

A6_dev_no_tf.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
A6_dev_no_tf.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); SLG-Net's heads add little; + pre-flight, image cache and the oracle predictions
A6_dev_no_tf.about: Paper A fold-0 development (Analysis/06 §4). D1: as A6_dev_base without teacher forcing (the heads always see the predicted mask). Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the oracle test.

A6_dev_detach.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
A6_dev_detach.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); SLG-Net's heads add little; + pre-flight, image cache and the oracle predictions
A6_dev_detach.about: Paper A fold-0 development (Analysis/06 §4). D2: as A6_dev_base, but the decision losses do not reach the mask (it is learned from the mask loss only). Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the oracle test.

A6_dev_scale32.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
A6_dev_scale32.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); SLG-Net's heads add little; + pre-flight, image cache and the oracle predictions
A6_dev_scale32.about: Paper A fold-0 development (Analysis/06 §4). D3: as A6_dev_base with region pooling at 1/32 only. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the oracle test.

A_dev_round1.about: Paper A fold-0 development, round 1 (Analysis/06 §4): A6_dev_base on GPU 0 and A6_dev_no_tf on GPU 1, in one session. Both results are in results_A_dev_round1.zip.

A_dev_round2.about: Paper A fold-0 development, round 2 (Analysis/06 §4): A6_dev_detach on GPU 0 and A6_dev_scale32 on GPU 1, in one session.

A6_dev_base_s2.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
A6_dev_base_s2.estimate_note: A_dev_round1 and A_dev_round2 took about 52 and 51 min (register lines 13-16)
A6_dev_base_s2.about: Paper A second-seed check (Analysis/06 §10): A6_dev_base repeated with seed 2027 (the first round used seed 2026); everything else identical. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the oracle test.

A6_dev_scale32_s2.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
A6_dev_scale32_s2.estimate_note: A_dev_round1 and A_dev_round2 took about 52 and 51 min (register lines 13-16)
A6_dev_scale32_s2.about: Paper A second-seed check (Analysis/06 §10): A6_dev_scale32 (region pooling at 1/32 only) repeated with seed 2027 (the first round used seed 2026); everything else identical. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the oracle test.

A_dev_seed2.about: Paper A second-seed check (Analysis/06 §10), asked for by the person on 2026-11-27 together with the final runs: A6_dev_base_s2 on GPU 0 and A6_dev_scale32_s2 on GPU 1, in one session, launched from main. Analysis C11 applies the rule of Analysis/06 §10 to the mean of the two seeds.

R00_reference_bank.about: Paper B step B-1 (Analysis/07_Step4_PaperB_Reference_Bank_Protocol.md). Trains nothing: encodes every femur, as released and mirrored, with the frozen ImageNet weights of M0's backbone, picks each femur's healthy references from the bank of each of the 5 fold models, and runs the sanity checks (mirror check, retrieval vs chance, duplicates, held-out vs test, partner rank) with a nearest-neighbour figure. Writes pairs.csv and references.csv, which every R run will read.
R00_reference_bank.estimate_note: about 2 min to build the image cache, under 1 min of features on a T4, about 1 min of checks

R00_reference_bank_r2.about: Paper B step B-1, version 2 of the orientation rule (Analysis/07 §8): the same bank, exclusion, features and checks as R00_reference_bank, but each reference is mirrored when its pelvis side (read from the image) differs from the femur's, instead of when the ImageNet features prefer it (those features hardly see left and right: check 1 was 58.4%). Its pairs.csv and references.csv are the ones every R run reads.
R00_reference_bank_r2.estimate_note: R00_reference_bank took 2.46 min on a T4 (register line 17); the side rule adds under a second

A2_region.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
A2_region.about: Paper A final run A2 (Analysis/06 §7 and §9, settings frozen by analysis C06: teacher forcing over 30 epochs, end-to-end mask, region pooling at 1/32 only): M0 + region pooling (C2) at 1/32: a flat 6-class head on [c, r]. Answers: does looking inside the predicted region help?. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag A-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "A-v1-frozen").
A2_region.estimate_note: M0 (S10) took 140 min on T4 x2 (register line 8); the SLG-Net development runs took 49-52 min for fold 0 on one T4 against M0's 44.5 min, so about 10% more

A3_geometry.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
A3_geometry.about: Paper A final run A3 (Analysis/06 §7 and §9, settings frozen by analysis C06: teacher forcing over 30 epochs, end-to-end mask, region pooling at 1/32 only): M0 + region geometry (C3): 8 numbers of the predicted region. Answers: does the region's shape and position help?. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag A-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "A-v1-frozen").
A3_geometry.estimate_note: M0 (S10) took 140 min on T4 x2 (register line 8); the SLG-Net development runs took 49-52 min for fold 0 on one T4 against M0's 44.5 min, so about 10% more

A4_hierarchy.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
A4_hierarchy.about: Paper A final run A4 (Analysis/06 §7 and §9, settings frozen by analysis C06: teacher forcing over 30 epochs, end-to-end mask, region pooling at 1/32 only): M0 + fracture -> location -> grade heads (C4), one grade trunk per location. Answers: does deciding location first, then grade, help?. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag A-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "A-v1-frozen").
A4_hierarchy.estimate_note: M0 (S10) took 140 min on T4 x2 (register line 8); the SLG-Net development runs took 49-52 min for fold 0 on one T4 against M0's 44.5 min, so about 10% more

A5_shared_grade.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
A5_shared_grade.about: Paper A final run A5 (Analysis/06 §7 and §9, settings frozen by analysis C06: teacher forcing over 30 epochs, end-to-end mask, region pooling at 1/32 only): M0 + one shared severity trunk (C5). Answers: does sharing one grade trunk help Garden I-II?. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag A-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "A-v1-frozen").
A5_shared_grade.estimate_note: M0 (S10) took 140 min on T4 x2 (register line 8); the SLG-Net development runs took 49-52 min for fold 0 on one T4 against M0's 44.5 min, so about 10% more

A6_slgnet.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
A6_slgnet.about: Paper A final run A6 (Analysis/06 §7 and §9, settings frozen by analysis C06: teacher forcing over 30 epochs, end-to-end mask, region pooling at 1/32 only): M0 + logit adjustment (C6) = SLG-Net, with both interpretability tests (oracle and region deletion). Answers: does it help the rare classes? Paper A's main model. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag A-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "A-v1-frozen").
A6_slgnet.estimate_note: M0 (S10) took 140 min on T4 x2 (register line 8); the SLG-Net development runs took 49-52 min for fold 0 on one T4 against M0's 44.5 min, so about 10% more; the deletion test predicts every held-out and test femur twice more

R4_dev_base.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
R4_dev_base.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); R4 also encodes 3 references per femur without gradients, about 1.6 times M0's step (Analysis/08 §5); + pre-flight, image cache and the self and random tests
R4_dev_base.about: Paper B fold-0 development (Analysis/08 §4). RefFrac R4 with the base settings of Analysis/08 §2: the 3 nearest healthy references of R00_reference_bank_r2, local cross-attention within ±1/8 of the image height at 1/16 and 1/32, difference fusion, no margin loss, seed 2026. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the tests self and random (Analysis/08 §2.6).

R4_dev_base_s2.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
R4_dev_base_s2.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); R4 also encodes 3 references per femur without gradients, about 1.6 times M0's step (Analysis/08 §5); + pre-flight, image cache and the self and random tests
R4_dev_base_s2.about: Paper B fold-0 development (Analysis/08 §4): R4_dev_base repeated with seed 2027; everything else identical. The mean of the two seeds is the base of analysis C12, and their difference in Dice is its seed noise N. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the tests self and random (Analysis/08 §2.6).

R4_dev_global.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
R4_dev_global.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); R4 also encodes 3 references per femur without gradients, about 1.6 times M0's step (Analysis/08 §5); + pre-flight, image cache and the self and random tests
R4_dev_global.about: Paper B fold-0 development (Analysis/08 §4). D1: as R4_dev_base, but the attention sees every position of the references (no local window). Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the tests self and random (Analysis/08 §2.6).

R4_dev_margin.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
R4_dev_margin.estimate_note: M0's fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4 (S10, register line 8); R4 also encodes 3 references per femur without gradients, about 1.6 times M0's step (Analysis/08 §5); + pre-flight, image cache and the self and random tests
R4_dev_margin.about: Paper B fold-0 development (Analysis/08 §4). D2: as R4_dev_base, plus AASN's margin loss at weight 0.5 (Analysis/08 §2.4). Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions; with the tests self and random (Analysis/08 §2.6).

R_dev_round1.about: Paper B fold-0 development, round 1 (Analysis/08 §4): R4_dev_base on GPU 0 and R4_dev_base_s2 on GPU 1, in one session, launched from main. Analysis C12 uses the mean of the two seeds as the base and their difference as the seed noise.

R_dev_round2.about: Paper B fold-0 development, round 2 (Analysis/08 §4): R4_dev_global (D1) on GPU 0 and R4_dev_margin (D2) on GPU 1, in one session, launched from main. Analysis C12 compares each with the base of round 1.

R4_refrac.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
R4_refrac.about: Paper B final run R4 (Analysis/08 §1, §2 and §5; settings frozen by analysis C12: 60 epochs, M0's recipe, the references of R00_reference_bank_r2, local window ±1/8 of the image height, no margin loss unless the variant has one): RefFrac, the main method: the 3 nearest healthy references, local cross-attention at 1/16 and 1/32, difference fusion [T, T-R, |T-R|]. With the reference tests self and random. Answers RQ-B1 with R2 and R3, and is the reference of every other R run. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag B-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "B-v1-frozen").
R4_refrac.estimate_note: measured: an R4 fold took 81 min on one T4 in the development runs (81 s per epoch; register lines 27-30), so 3 rounds of folds on T4 x2 + the test set in 3 modes + set-up

R3_nearest_ref.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
R3_nearest_ref.about: Paper B final run R3 (Analysis/08 §1, §2 and §5; settings frozen by analysis C12: 60 epochs, M0's recipe, the references of R00_reference_bank_r2, local window ±1/8 of the image height, no margin loss unless the variant has one): as R4 with only the nearest healthy reference (k = 1). R3 vs R2: does retrieval help?; R4 vs R3: do 3 references help? With the reference tests self and random. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag B-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "B-v1-frozen").
R3_nearest_ref.estimate_note: estimate: one reference instead of three; no k = 1 run timed on a T4 yet (an R4 fold took 81 min, M0's 45 min); 3 rounds of folds on T4 x2 + the test set in every mode + set-up

R2_random_ref.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
R2_random_ref.about: Paper B final run R2 (Analysis/08 §1, §2 and §5; settings frozen by analysis C12: 60 epochs, M0's recipe, the references of R00_reference_bank_r2, local window ±1/8 of the image height, no margin loss unless the variant has one): as R3, but the reference is a random healthy femur of the fold model's bank (fixed per femur in the table). Does any healthy second image help? With the reference tests self and random. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag B-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "B-v1-frozen").
R2_random_ref.estimate_note: estimate: one reference instead of three; no k = 1 run timed on a T4 yet (an R4 fold took 81 min, M0's 45 min); 3 rounds of folds on T4 x2 + the test set in every mode + set-up

R7_partner.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
R7_partner.about: Paper B final run R7 (Analysis/08 §1, §2 and §5; settings frozen by analysis C12: 60 epochs, M0's recipe, the references of R00_reference_bank_r2, local window ±1/8 of the image height, no margin loss unless the variant has one): as R3, but trained with the femur's own healthy partner from the same x-ray (mirrored), else the nearest. Own hip vs retrieved (RQ-B2) and the pairing shortcut (RQ-B3, §2.5), with the test modes blind, retrieved, random and fractured. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag B-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "B-v1-frozen").
R7_partner.estimate_note: estimate: one reference instead of three; no k = 1 run timed on a T4 yet (an R4 fold took 81 min, M0's 45 min); 3 rounds of folds on T4 x2 + the test set in every mode + set-up

R1_aasn.gpu: T4 x2 (two folds at a time)
R1_aasn.about: Paper B final run R1 (Analysis/08 §1, §2 and §5; settings frozen by analysis C12: 60 epochs, M0's recipe, the references of R00_reference_bank_r2, local window ±1/8 of the image height, no margin loss unless the variant has one): the closest published idea (AASN), adapted to femur crops (§2.4): the nearest healthy reference, a global affine alignment, concatenation and AASN's margin loss (weight 0.5). With the reference tests self and random. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from the tag B-v1-frozen (BRANCH = "B-v1-frozen").

A1_m0_deletion.about: Paper A, analysis C08: M0 (= A1) trained again exactly as S10 (same settings and seed), now with the region-deletion test of Analysis/06 §5, so that SLG-Net's deletion result can be compared with M0's by the rule of Analysis/06 §13, fixed before this run. M0's head never sees the mask, so it has no oracle test. 5 folds and the test set. Launch from main (BRANCH = "main") after the pull request that adds it.

N_segzoom_fold0.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
N_segzoom_fold0.estimate_note: ConvNeXt U-Net fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4; the zoom encoder adds about 0.6 of that, plus the full-resolution image cache and data loading
N_segzoom_fold0.about: Screening of method candidate 1 (Analysis/11, section 'Fold-0 screening rules'): the segment-and-zoom network. The ConvNeXt U-Net finds the fracture on the image at half resolution, and a second ConvNeXt-T grades it from a 640 x 640 full-resolution crop around the predicted mask (input 1536 x 1024, teacher forcing of the crop centre over 30 epochs). Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions.

N_res1152_fold0.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)
N_res1152_fold0.estimate_note: ConvNeXt U-Net fold 0 trained in 44.5 min on one T4; 2.25 times the pixels, so about 1.9 times the time
N_res1152_fold0.about: Screening of method candidate 2 (Analysis/11, section 'Fold-0 screening rules'): the ConvNeXt U-Net unchanged, at 1152 x 768 instead of 768 x 512 (1.5 times the resolution). Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions.

N_convnext_s_fold0.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)

N_convnext_s_fold0.about: Screening of method candidate 3 (Analysis/11, section 'Fold-0 screening rules'): the ConvNeXt U-Net with the larger ConvNeXt-S encoder (ImageNet-22k weights) at 768 x 512. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions.

N_segzoom_fold0_seed2.gpu: one T4 (started by a parallel group, one run per GPU)

N_segzoom_fold0_seed2.about: Screening of method candidate 1 (Analysis/11, section 'Fold-0 screening rules'): the segment-and-zoom network. Second seed (2027) of the same run, for the pass rule's mean of two seeds. Fold 0 only, no test-set predictions.
